Normality test for Column A1 (n = 35)
=====================================
Descriptive statistics:
  Mean            = 406.703434
  Std (sample)    = 0.020885
  Std (pop)       = 0.020584
  Min / Max       = 406.6703 / 406.7344
  Range           = 0.0641
  Skewness        = -0.1546
  Excess kurtosis = -1.5003

Normality tests (H0: data are normally distributed; alpha = 0.05):
  Shapiro-Wilk        W = 0.9079,  p = 0.0065  -> REJECT H0 (NOT normal)
  Kolmogorov-Smirnov  D = 0.1661,  p = 0.2588  -> fail to reject H0
  Anderson-Darling    A2 = 1.2116  (5% crit = 0.735) -> REJECT H0 (NOT normal)

Conclusion: Column A1 does NOT follow a normal distribution.
  - The Shapiro-Wilk test rejects normality (p = 0.0065 < 0.05).
  - The Anderson-Darling statistic (1.2116) exceeds the 5% critical value (0.735), also rejecting normality.
  - The distribution is slightly left-skewed (skew = -0.15) and clearly platykurtic (excess kurtosis = -1.50, i.e. flatter / lighter tails than a normal distribution), which is consistent with the data being tightly clustered around the mean (~406.703) within a very narrow range of 0.064.
  - Only the K-S test fails to reject (it has lower power than Shapiro-Wilk for small n); the stronger tests (Shapiro-Wilk and Anderson-Darling) agree that the data deviate from normality.
